title: Leave loading and support retry after a failure
contract: Implement reduceRequest(state, action) with items,status,activeRequestId,error. pending records requestId, sets loading and clears any error. Only the active request can fulfill or reject. fulfilled stores action.items and succeeded; rejected stores failed and action.error, or "Request failed" if missing. An aborted active rejection returns idle with no error. All terminal states clear activeRequestId and preserve prior items on failure/abort. Unknown and stale events do nothing. Inputs are frozen.
hints: Every active pending request needs a terminal success, failure or cancellation transition.
Preserve previous rows on failure, clear the error when retrying, and ignore failures from stale requests.

tests.name: A network failure ends loading and preserves rows
tests.explanation: The user needs a failed state and error instead of an infinite spinner.

tests.name: Retry clears the error and can recover successfully
tests.explanation: A fresh request can recover without hard-refreshing the dashboard.

tests.name: Cancellation is not shown as a network failure
tests.explanation: An intentional cancellation returns to idle without an error.

tests.name: An old rejection cannot fail a newer pending request
tests.explanation: Failure handling needs the same request ownership guard as success.

tests.name: Missing error text has a useful fallback
tests.explanation: A rejected request must have a visible failure message.

businessContext: A network drop or 503 gateway timeout occurs. The UI skeleton spinner spins indefinitely, the table is unclickable, and the user must hard-refresh the page to regain control.
productionSymptom: Users report an infinite spinning wheel on the loan dashboard during transient Wi-Fi drops.
